name: Ottoman Empire - Selim I
startIntroPart1: Sultan Selim, called Yavuz, the Grim: in eight years you doubled the lands of Osman. Chaldiran broke the Safavid line, Marj Dabiq and Ridaniya swallowed the Mamluks whole, and the keys of Mecca and Medina were carried to your tent.
startIntroPart2: The soldiers are mustered and the road is open. Will you ride it to the ends of the earth?
declaringWar: I have no use for your embassies. The army is already marching.
attacked: You raise a hand against me? Then I will take your cities and your name with them.
defeated: So the sword has turned. Take the empire; you will not hold it long.
denounced: Your word is worth nothing, and I will say so before every court.
introduction: I am Selim, son of Bayezid, Sultan of the Two Lands and Khakan of the Two Seas. Speak briefly.
hateHello: You still draw breath. Be quick about it.
tradeRequest: Here are my terms. I do not expect to repeat them.
uniques: [+15]% Production when constructing [Military] units [in all cities]

name: Ottoman Empire - Mehmed II
startIntroPart1: Sultan Mehmed, called Fatih, the Conqueror: at twenty-one you took the city that had turned away every army for a thousand years. The great bombards did it, and you had them cast yourself.
startIntroPart2: You founded the Sahn-i Seman so that the empire would be taught as well as armed. Will learning carry you further than the cannon did?
declaringWar: Walls are a problem of engineering. I have solved harder ones.
attacked: A poor calculation. Let me show you the arithmetic.
defeated: The city is lost. What was built here will outlast you.
denounced: I have measured you, and found you wanting.
introduction: I am Mehmed, Kayser-i Rum, master of Konstantiniyye. My court holds scholars of every faith. Perhaps you have something to teach me.
hateHello: I have read your intentions already.
tradeRequest: A proposal. Examine it closely; it is better than it looks.
uniques: [+25]% Production when constructing [Siege] units [in all cities]

name: Ottoman Empire - Suleiman I
startIntroPart1: Sultan Suleiman, called Kanuni, the Lawgiver, and Magnificent by those who had to look at your court: Sinan raised your mosques, Baki wrote your verses, and the law you codified outlived every wall you built.
startIntroPart2: An age is remembered for what it made, not what it took. What will yours be remembered for?
declaringWar: I would rather have built something here. Since you insist, the army is ready.
attacked: This was beneath you. It will not be forgotten.
defeated: The empire falls. The law and the verses remain.
denounced: A ruler is bound by his own law first. You are bound by nothing.
introduction: From Topkapi, greetings. I am Suleiman. My court welcomes poets, architects and honest envoys. I hope you are one of the three.
hateHello: I had hoped for better from you.
tradeRequest: An arrangement, fairly drawn. Read it at your leisure.

name: Ottoman Empire - Selim III
startIntroPart1: Sultan Selim, composer and reformer: you sent the first permanent ambassadors to London, Paris, Vienna and Berlin, and opened the Muhendishane so that Ottoman officers could learn what Europe had learned.
startIntroPart2: The Nizam-i Cedid, the New Order, cost you the throne. Will the world listen to you this time?
declaringWar: Every channel has been tried. I regret what follows.
attacked: You chose force over conversation. That tells me everything.
defeated: The New Order ends here. Someone will try again.
denounced: I will put this before every court in the world, and let them judge.
introduction: I am Selim, third of the name. I would rather send you an ambassador than an army. Shall we begin properly?
hateHello: My ambassadors have been recalled. You know why.
tradeRequest: My envoys have drawn this up. I believe it serves us both.
uniques: Resting point for Influence with City-States is increased by [10]
Gifts of Gold to City-States generate [25]% more Influence
Allied City-States provide [Science] equal to [25]% of what they produce for themselves

name: Ottoman Empire - Bayezid II
startIntroPart1: Sultan Bayezid, called Veli, the Saint: when Spain expelled the Sephardim in 1492 you sent the fleet to carry them here, and asked how a king could call himself wise while impoverishing his own country and enriching yours.
startIntroPart2: You ruled over Muslims, Christians and Jews alike and let each keep their law. Can an empire be held together by tolerance?
declaringWar: I have exhausted my patience, which was considerable.
attacked: I offered you peace. You will find I am not defenceless.
defeated: Protect the people who came here for refuge. That is all I ask.
denounced: You mistake forbearance for weakness. Many have.
introduction: Peace be upon you. I am Bayezid. In my lands a man may keep his own faith and his own courts. Perhaps that is strange to you.
hateHello: I will hear you out. I promise nothing more.
tradeRequest: An honest exchange, offered in good faith.
uniques: [+1 Happiness] [in all cities] <in cities following our religion>
[-25]% Faith cost of generating Great Prophet equivalents
